newsitem.title: UK: GUS says H1 profits to be one percent lower.
newsitem.headline: GUS says H1 profits to be one percent lower.

text.p: British retailer Great Universal Stores said on Friday pre-tax profit for the first six months would be around one percent lower than in the same period last year.

"The profit increases made by other divisions have not fully compensated for the lower outturn in UK home shopping and the adverse movement of the South African rand," said Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale at the company's annual meeting.
Shares in GUS dropped 17-1/2 pence to 617p by 1110 GMT.
UK home shopping has experienced an approximate three percent fall in demand "in a very competitive market" and the slide in profits comes despite a marginal rise in group sales.
Pre-tax profits for the six months to September 30 1995 were 237.5 million stg versus 226.8 million stg the year before.
